text: The big storyline heading into Sunday's divisional clash with the Jets centers on A.J. Brown's availability, as the Patriots activated the wide receiver from injured reserve Saturday following a four-game absence with a right high ankle sprain, though head coach Mike Vrabel will make a final decision on his status, and Brown himself acknowledged things remain "still up in the air"—meanwhile, Christian Gonzalez is expected to play, and the team elevated safety Elliott Davison from the practice squad for the matchup. On the brighter side, tight end Hunter Henry was named the NFLPA's Community MVP for Week 6 after hosting his second annual "Freedom to Play" ping pong tournament, continuing a strong week of community recognition after teammate Mack Hollins earned the same honor two weeks prior. The Patriots arrive as a team riding their best performance of the season following a dominant 28-point victory, though they'll face a Jets squad that recognizes the significance of this divisional game, with receiver Garrett Wilson calling it a "big-ass game" for New York's playoff positioning, and the team will have to account for Geno Smith's impressive stretch without an interception.
